newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European Commission acts over clipped oats dispute.
newsitem.headline: European Commission acts over clipped oats dispute.

text.p: The European Commission has decided to press ahead with a regulation on durum wheat imports even though its GATT dispute over clipped oats with Canada has not been resolved, an EU official said on Wednesday.

"Talks between the Commission and Canada over the issue of clipped oats have failed to resolve the issue and the Commission now feels that it is in breach of its GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) obligations," the official said.
European Union cereals experts will discuss on Thursday a draft implementing regulations covering durum wheat imports under the GATT Article 24/6 agreement on EU enlargment.
Canada has been blocking progress because it says it wants to include quality criteria which would favour its own clipped oats exports.
"With the talks with Canada stalled the Commission has decided to introduce a regulation covering the annual 50,000 tonne quota for durum wheat for 1996/97.
"It is also proposing a regulation covering the half year from January 1 to June 30 which is the first period after the agreement was signed," the official said.
The Commission proposal omits the annual quota of 10,000 tonnes of clipped or processed oats covered by the Article 24/6 agreement.
The issue is listed for a vote at the EU's cereals management committee after the experts meeting.
